gap: No result ChatGPT got turns the makers' 'standby' and 'self-consumption' figures and the testers' '% lost per hour' results into one number: watts drawn with only the DC side on. Measured that way by the same reviewer, BLUETTI's own Elite 30 V2 draws about 11 W with DC on, not the 4.5 W BLUETTI advertises. The BLUETTI EB3A, which ChatGPT told DC-only shoppers to avoid, draws about 3.6 W.
standout_why: Compared against powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-standby-draw (cited), wattpowerstation.com small-loads (cited), outagemath.com/appliances/wifi-router (cited), en.best-batteries.com 46 measurements (cited) and thetechnologyman.com EB3A review (cited). powerstations.reviews lists 41 maker figures under five different names ('self-consumption', 'standby power consumption', 'idle power consumption', 'active idle power', 'no-load consumption'). It never says which outputs were on, and it gives the Elite 30 V2 as 9 W while BLUETTI's US store says 4.5 W. wattpowerstation has one DC-only figure (DELTA Pro 3, about 13 W, Hobotech) and nothing for small units. outagemath assumes the draw and says makers don't publish it. Best Batteries gives USB-C and 12 V Wh with no load stated. The Technology Man EB3A page gives only '16% in 12 hours', never watts, so ChatGPT read it as a warning. None puts DC-on watts for two small stations side by side on one method.
decides: It changes the DC-only pick and corrects ChatGPT's advice. With a 15 W router on the 12 V port, the Elite 30 V2's measured 11 W of DC-on draw nearly doubles the load: about 11 h from 288 Wh (288 ÷ 26 W). Its own 4.5 W claim would suggest about 15 h (288 ÷ 19.5 W). For low DC loads, the advertised standby number can't be used to rank stations. DC-on draw measured by a reviewer is the column that decides it. The EcoFlow TRAIL '0.01 W no-load' figure is a storage/sleep figure, not DC-on draw: EcoFlow gives it with no condition, next to '≤5% a month'. So it can't be ranked against the others either. The Anker C300 DC's 94.8% is an AC-port test of the C300X DC with no load stated, so it doesn't support ChatGPT's 'best for DC-only' claim.
